_provenance: Re-baselined 2026-10-07 for D-100. `_mark_informational_if_multi_energy` was removed — it re-characterized the proposed model inside the determination to decide whether AHJ-1 and AHJ-3 had fired, a second source of truth beside the disclosure branch that already knew — so its `article=article` warn site retires and the bare `article` key goes from 18 warn uses to 17. The generic collector's determination warning appears as a new dynamic key joining the FIRED entries' own articles, with warn 1: one key retires, one appears, and no citation is lost. The collector cites the articles the rule sites recorded rather than one hardcoded article, which is the point of the change.

Re-baselined 2026-10-08 for Sol's `129`.5. The System 5 presence decision cited `8.4.4.1.(5); Table 8.4.4.7.-B` as a LITERAL, so a necb2025 run told an authority its AHJ-11 condition came from the other edition's articles. Both branches now derive the citation from the edition's own `reference_subsection`, which is why four per-edition literal counts drop by one each: 2020/8.4.4.1 and 2020/8.4.4.7 cited 5->4 and 6->5, and the 2025 counterparts the same. Nothing is lost from the PRODUCT — the citation is now correct for both editions rather than correct for one — but a literal-only per-edition scanner can no longer see it, which is the same trade every other prefix-derived citation in this file already made. One dynamic key is added, `presence_article`; it is a NAME, so the foreign scanner counts it conservatively rather than inspecting its content, and the unheated branch's inline f-string cites only Section 8.4 articles and so is not foreign at all. Verified end to end in the frozen full-year determination-02 run: the AHJ-11 condition carries '8.4.5.1.(5); Table 8.4.5.7.-B'.

Re-baselined 2026-10-08 for Fable's `131` F6. Three citations in reference.py stopped spelling NECB 2020's subsection as a literal and now derive the run's own: the D-28 multizone merge decision's `Table 8.4.x.7.-B Note (3)`, and the humidification capture decision and orphan warning's `Table 8.4.x.7.-B Note (1)`. Each becomes a DYNAMIC site, which this scanner counts conservatively because it cannot inspect the content — the same treatment `presence_article` got, and the reason the total rises by three (187 to 190) for citations that are not foreign at all: every one resolves wholly inside Section 8.4. The static halves they replaced are gone from the other baseline for the same edit.

Re-baselined 2026-10-08 for Fable's `133` G3. The economizer pair's mixed literal `'8.4.4.12.; 5.2.2.7.(1)'` becomes a dynamic citation, so its two static sites leave this file and the derived form is counted conservatively instead — the same trade the two entries above made. The 5.2.2.7 half, which is what makes it foreign, is unchanged and still cited.
Re-baselined 2026-10-08 for issue #72: the scanner now resolves manifest-looked-up citations, so sites that were invisible to BOTH gates are counted again here too.

Re-baselined 2026-10-09 for D-101 and Sol's `143`: AHJ-3's plant cardinality question left the AHJ-1 allocation disclosure and is emitted as its own plant-scoped record, adding one dynamic `article=sentence_six` warn site. AHJ-1 now dedupes on the SERVICE SET rather than the plant, because two proposed serving systems drawing on one dual-fuel plant are two 8.4.x.9.(5) allocation choices and the plant key emitted a single warning for both.

Re-baselined 2026-10-09 for Sol's `143` blockers 4 and 5: the post-selection merge audit split by note — Table 8.4.x.7.-B Note (3) for System 6, Note (2) for Systems 1/2/5, which is what the table marks on them — so the Note (3) key is re-spelled against a local `subsection` and a Note (2) key joins it; and the Data Processing cooling threshold now declares whether it measured the block or the serving system, adding one warn site on `rule['article']`.
